tldr: Wealthsimple launched Penny, an AI assistant that can take actions across banking and trading, while BMO put agentic AI into its credit card contact centre and Anthropic added a personal finance tool to Claude. Elsewhere, Nequi launched yield-bearing savings pockets, and crypto outages and Pix downtime in Brazil put third-party dependency and reliability in focus.
themes: Agentic AI in banking and trading

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple launches Penny, an AI assistant that can prepare e-transfers, pay invoices, flag duplicate card charges and help self-directed investors buy and sell. It never acts without client confirmation, and it connects to ChatGPT and Claude.
highlights.why: A direct competitor now offers an assistant that takes actions across banking and trading, not just answers questions. It sets a new bar for digital self-serve experiences, and the confirm-before-acting design and the ChatGPT/Claude links are worth studying.

highlights.headline: Anthropic adds a personal finance tool to Claude that lets users connect bank and card accounts and ask questions about their money.
highlights.why: General-purpose AI assistants are moving into money management, so customers may start asking questions about their finances outside our app. We should decide how we show up in those channels.

highlights.headline: BMO rolls out AI Agent Assist in its Virtual Connect contact centre. The internal agentic tool does transaction matching, policy retrieval and case preparation, and targets up to 30% shorter call times.
highlights.why: A big-bank peer is using agentic AI to speed up credit card service. This is a benchmark for service-cost and resolution-time targets, and the rollout is limited to agent-assist, with no customer-facing agent yet.

highlights.headline: Nubank and Mercado Pago suspended crypto deposits and withdrawals after an external verification provider failed. Separate Pix outages hit Banco do Brasil and affected other banks.
highlights.why: The outages show how a single third-party vendor can freeze a core feature. It is a useful prompt to review our vendor dependencies, failover plans and customer communication during incidents.
